name: Tekirdağ
title: Tekirdağ Ship Thickness Measurement | Bulk, Tanker UTM
description: Ship thickness gauging in Tekirdağ for bulk carriers, edible-oil tankers, container ships and LNG carriers: UTM of holds, tanks, decks and piping.
h1: Ship Gauging at Tekirdağ: Thickness Measurement on the Thracian Coast
intro: Tekirdağ sits on the northern shore of the Sea of Marmara in Turkish Thrace, and its terminals serve the factories, farms and gas network of the surrounding region. Bulk carriers bring grain and raw materials, tankers load and discharge edible oils and fuel, container ships call at a deep-water terminal and LNG carriers deliver gas along the coast. Many stay long enough to gauge. Technicians travel from India to the vessel, working at berth or at the open anchorages off the town.

highlights.p: Handysize and Supramax bulk carriers bringing grain, oilseeds and feed to Thracian processors empty their holds in a day or two. Once clean, hold frames, tank tops and hatch coamings can be gauged.
Small tankers carrying vegetable oils and refined products suit careful tank gauging between parcels, with tank coatings and heating coils a frequent reason for a closer look at the steel.

highlights.h: A deep-water container and gas coast
highlights.p: The container terminal and the LNG receiving jetty bring regular scheduled calls. Ballast tanks, deck and hatch structure can be gauged on those visits, with cargo spaces treated according to their own rules.

port.h: Tekirdağ and the north Marmara coast
p: Tekirdağ is the provincial centre of Turkish Thrace, on the north shore of the Sea of Marmara roughly midway between the Dardanelles and the Bosphorus. The town has a municipal port, and along the coast to the east and west lie private terminals built for the industrial belt that runs inland through Çorlu and Çerkezköy. There is no natural harbour sheltering the whole coast, so berths are protected by breakwaters and ships at anchor are exposed to the Marmara's winter northerlies, which can interrupt launch transfers for days at a time.

The cargo mix is unusually varied for a small coast. Grain, oilseeds, fertiliser and feed arrive in bulk for the region's food and agricultural industries, and vegetable oils move in small chemical and product tankers. A deep-water container terminal calls feeders and larger ships, steel products and general cargo pass through the town's own quays, and gas arrives by LNG carrier at a terminal on the shore towards Marmara Ereğlisi. For a superintendent, that means a handful of ship types stopping within a short stretch of coast, many on regular patterns.

Most ships stay at the berth for a day or two, which is too short for a full survey but long enough for a focused programme. Bulk carriers that have discharged have clean holds at last, and coating condition, frame wastage and tank top plating can be read directly. Tankers carrying vegetable oil have tanks that are cleaned to a high standard between parcels, which makes entry and gauging simpler than on some other products. The coast has no repair yard of its own, so docking and steel renewal normally happen elsewhere on the Marmara, with Tekirdağ readings informing that plan.

facilities.h: Where gauging is realistic at Tekirdağ
p: Gauging here is done alongside, under the access and safety rules of each terminal. At the bulk and general cargo quays, holds are measured once discharged and cleaned, with frames, hopper and tank top plating and hatch coamings on the list. At the liquid berths, certified ballast tanks, deck plating and deck piping are the usual scope, and cargo tanks are entered only when a parcel is finished and the tanks are gas-free and certified. The container terminal allows ballast tanks, hatch covers and deck structure to be reached between cargo operations.

Ships waiting for a berth or for orders anchor off the town, and a launch can be arranged by the agent when the sea is calm enough. In the Marmara's less settled weather the agent's judgement decides whether a launch transfer is sensible, so the team plans a short, prioritised scope and is ready to drop it if the swell rises. For a drydock the ship goes to a yard elsewhere in the Marmara, and pre-docking readings from Tekirdağ shorten the planning at the other end.
list: Bulk and general cargo quays at the town port — holds, hatch coamings, deck and tank tops on ships once discharged and cleaned
Edible-oil and fuel jetties — certified ballast tanks, deck plating and deck piping on small tankers between parcels
Deep-water container terminal — ballast tanks, hatch covers and deck structure on feeders and larger ships between cargo operations
LNG receiving jetty towards Marmara Ereğlisi — deck, ballast tanks and engine room piping on carriers, with cargo containment left untouched
Open anchorage off Tekirdağ — condition gauging on ships awaiting a berth or orders, reached by launch when the sea allows
Docking elsewhere on the Marmara — Tekirdağ readings carried into a yard's steel estimate

context.h: Port state control and regional trade
p: Ships at Tekirdağ fall under the Black Sea MoU and Mediterranean MoU port state control regimes that Turkey belongs to, enforced through the local harbour master and the Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure. Bulk carriers and general cargo ships on short regional trades attract attention for hold condition, hatch cover sealing and corroded ventilators, and an unannounced inspection can turn a vague concern about wastage into a firm request for readings. The coast sees older tonnage regularly, and owners who keep up a gauging record often find it useful when an inspector asks for evidence.

The trades that feed Tekirdağ are tied to the Thracian economy: processors of sunflower and other oilseeds, flour and feed mills, the factory belt around Çorlu and a gas network supplied through the LNG jetty. Owners of ships working those trades range from large Turkish bulk fleets to small family companies running coasters, and their technical departments are often lean, which makes a clear gauging report with marked-up compartments especially useful. Voyages that continue to EU ports bring Inventory of Hazardous Materials requirements and carbon-reporting duties.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Tekirdağ
jobs.p: Work at Tekirdağ mostly follows cargo discharge. When holds or tanks are empty and certified, a superintendent can take the opportunity to measure a compartment that is normally full. Scopes are set by the cargo and the schedule, and several jobs are linked to a docking at another Marmara yard. Others come from a purchase, a charterer's inspection request or a port state control finding in the previous port.
list: Hold frame, hopper plating and tank top gauging on a Handysize bulk carrier after grain discharge at the town quays.
Ballast and deck gauging on a small vegetable-oil tanker between parcels, followed by heating coil and tank bottom plate readings once the tanks are certified.
Hatch cover and coaming gauging on a general cargo ship after port state control noted wasted coamings at a Black Sea port.
Deck, ballast tank and engine room pipe readings on a container feeder during a scheduled call at the deep-water terminal.
Pre-docking gauging on an older bulk carrier at anchor, giving a Marmara yard a steel estimate before the ship is booked in.
Deck plating and ballast tank gauging on an LNG carrier at the receiving jetty, with the cargo containment system outside the scope.

logistics: The nearest airports with international service are in Istanbul, and the team reaches Tekirdağ by road along the Marmara coast, with Çorlu's regional airport an option for domestic connections. Terminal access is arranged through the ship's agent, who also books anchorage launches and relays the terminal's requirements for gas-free certificates and permits. Indian passport holders need a Turkish visa, so we apply as soon as the ship's call is nominated and ask the agent to warn us if the berth moves.

faqs.q: Can holds be gauged after grain discharge at Tekirdağ?
faqs.a: Yes, once the holds are discharged, swept and cleaned to the point where the crew can certify entry. Hold frames, hopper plating and tank tops are then readable by ultrasonic thickness measurement. We plan the work around the loading plan for the next cargo, so the holds are handed back to the crew in time.

Not for merchant ships of any size. Docking and steel renewal normally happen at yards elsewhere on the Marmara, such as Tuzla or the Yalova yards. Gauging done at Tekirdağ is reported in a form that can go straight to the yard as a steel estimate, which saves time once the ship is booked in.

faqs.q: What happens if the Marmara weather stops launch transfers?
faqs.a: The agent will not book a launch when the sea is unsafe, and we do not push the point. The scope is built so the most valuable readings come first and anything left over can be picked up at the next call or in dock. Berth work is not affected by launch weather in the same way.

faqs.q: Can you measure plating on an LNG carrier?
faqs.a: We can gauge deck plating, ballast tanks, engine room piping and other accessible steel on an LNG carrier at the receiving jetty, subject to the terminal's rules. Cargo containment structures are specialist items and outside our scope. The plan is agreed with the master and the terminal before anyone boards.
